subject.title: I updated Scrapling and the skill became hidden again

question: Should the latest Scrapling update remain hidden under the current content-policy/security rules, or should maintainers restore it as a false positive and adjust the update scanner workflow?
rationale: The source tree shows moderation visibility controls, but the decisive evidence is production scanner/audit data and policy intent that automation should not infer.

options.title: Review and restore if false positive
options.body: Inspect production moderation signals for the Scrapling update, restore visibility if the hold is unintended, and document the scanner/update rule that caused it.

options.title: Keep hidden under policy
options.body: Leave the package hidden if the update matches a disallowed or review-pending category, and explain the policy basis in the RFC or operator notes.

options.title: Define a durable update path
options.body: Change the product policy so trusted existing packages can update without repeated public-hiding holds unless a stronger scanner signal appears.

recommendation.title: Review and restore if false positive
recommendation.body: Inspect production moderation signals for the Scrapling update, restore visibility if the hold is unintended, and document the scanner/update rule that caused it.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick owns the related content-policy RFC that controls whether this visibility hold is expected or a false positive.
